title: RAW UNREVIEWED: physical-entry neutralization of two internal minim spelling classes
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. A fixed writer maps internal B_m to entry D_m while an internal D_m class remains D_m everywhere. Test exact repeated same-paragraph right-two and right-three complete-word signatures across physical leaves; predicted entry counterparts preserve minim length and every continuation word. No meaning, bare/D lexical identity, or line-only d rule is asserted.
access: Existing admitted GDT915 P-text snapshots only for a separately selected test. Producer opens no target rows, source lines, images or reserves. f84/f84r sealed; f116v not admitted; readers separate.

design.mechanism: Let m be exact one/two/three-i spelling, B_m=a+i^m+n, D_m=d+a+i^m+n. Two opaque internal construction classes B and D are retained: writer(B_m,internal)=B_m; writer(B_m,physical-entry)=D_m; writer(D_m,any)=D_m. This is a many-to-one entry spelling channel, not equality of the two internal lexical meanings. Internal D is therefore an expected observation, not an exception. Paragraph entries are a separate diagnostic scope.
design.unit: An exact target plus the next two, and separately next three, complete native groups within one source-marked paragraph. Signatures may cross physical lines within that paragraph. Preserve each whole native group, tail m, source physical leaf, paragraph and target position. No target or continuation spelling normalization and no reader pooling.
design.contrast: Entry neutralization versus (a) unchanged whole forms with break placement avoiding B, and (b) two independent internal word classes with an entry restriction but no promised cross-position counterpart. Signature n=2 and n=3 contracts are both frozen, never selected by observed yield. This is not IDEA000002 semantic owner-state persistence.
design.prediction: For every internal B_m plus exact right-n signature K, the corresponding physical-entry realization when the same construction recurs is D_m+K; every continuation word and m remain unchanged. Internal D_m+K can also produce entry D_m+K. Thus entry D signatures may combine both internal classes without proving their semantic equivalence. A raw-form equality endpoint is the complete target+K sequence after exactly this one directed entry rewrite, not similarity of neighbour distributions or a recount of zeros. Physical-leaf recurrence must be reported separately from same-paragraph recurrence, without selecting a successful K.
design.scope: Complete already admitted multiline native paragraphs, primary ZL3b and IT2a separately; ordinary continuation entries distinguished from paragraph starts. Frozen n=2 and n=3 signatures; keep all occurrences. Groups lacking n same-paragraph successors or containing unresolved native spelling remain explicit unavailable strata, never shortened to whatever window yields a match.
design.falsifier: A matched held construction whose entry realization changes tail m or any continuation word contradicts the fixed writer if the construction identity is independently warranted; no pair-specific replacement or exception is permitted. Exact opaque K alone may be ambiguous about construction identity, so a failed K match is not automatically linguistic refutation. A complete repeated sequence with stable B and shifted break instead supports the break-placement rival for that sequence. Missing exact recurrence is NO_CAPACITY, not failed neutralization. Exact context collisions of internal B and D do not themselves refute a many-to-one entry channel.
design.decision: Retain as raw fixed writing hypothesis, not a semantic reading. Before implementation root must freeze a counterpart contract and capacity without choosing signatures from observed success. If only union-of-contexts overlap appears, classify it as compatible but unidentifying: an unrestricted lexical-position rival reproduces it. A deterministic novel whole-form counterpart prediction can justify a bounded next writer experiment; absent capacity, stop rather than create a decoder or more glosses.

source_evidence.quote: The registered descriptive outcome is **MINIM_SPECIFIC_CONTINUATION_AVOIDANCE**. Bare `ain/aiin/aiiin` have zero starts even on physical continuation lines in complete multiline paragraphs. D forms do occur there; other a-initial forms supply exceptions to an absolute a-initial ban. This outcome name does **not** establish a statistically distinctive minim-specific mechanism: other a-initial words also strongly avoid this position. No meaning, silent d, shared lexical identity, or independent confirmation follows.

predecessors.difference: Complete continuation census establishes the positional constraint but neither a rewrite nor exact counterpart identity.

Failed crossed prediction of ain versus aiin from sparse adjacent whole words. This contract instead fixes minim length and predicts bare versus D target spelling for exact recurring larger signatures; it does not repair its classifier.
p/y same-lexeme shared decoding-key equality is a different contrast. Here B and D internal classes are allowed distinct, with entry coalescence rather than an asserted common lexeme.

The old teaching pair invents parameter/activated meaning from a small distribution sample. This contract adopts none of those meanings and requires exact full-word recurrence under one fixed directed writer.
Unspecified role operator on two diagram payload matches; present scope is exact minim tail and physical entry, with a fixed raw rewrite and no role endpoint.
Opaque-cell wrapper probabilities conditioned by line-start and preceding DY do not establish this deterministic class coalescence or same-construction counterpart.
Semantic owner/item persistence over wrap is not this raw spelling endpoint and is not a generic wrap-test precedent.

design.strongest_rival: Two independently lexicalized whole forms with a bare entry prohibition and memorized exact constructions can reproduce every observed counterpart. This blocks meaning selection and unconstrained equivalence claims, not retention of a raw writer contract.
